question: Node.js is single-threaded. What does a bulkhead's maxConcurrent actually limit, and why is that still a concurrency problem?
answer_hinglish:
`maxConcurrent` threads ko limit nahi karta -- woh limit karta hai ki ek dependency ke kitne calls ek saath IN FLIGHT hain, yaani kitne promises abhi settle nahi hue. Node ek thread pe JavaScript chalata hai, lekin I/O concurrent hota hai: 200 incoming requests aayi, har ek ne `fetch` kiya, toh 200 sockets ek saath khule hain aur 200 promises pending hain. Thread ek hai, concurrent calls 200.

Problem tab hota hai jab woh dependency hang karne lage. Har call timeout tak socket pakad ke baitha rehta hai, memory aur connection pool bharta jaata hai, aur doosri healthy dependencies ke calls ko bhi jagah nahi milti. Ek slow SMS provider poore process ko slow kar deta hai.

Bulkhead isko rokta hai: `Bulkhead({ maxConcurrent: 2 })` ka matlab hai is dependency ke maximum 2 calls ek saath chalenge. Teesra call ya toh queue mein wait karega (agar `maxQueue` > 0) ya turant `BulkheadRejectedError` paayega, bina operation chalaye. Toh hanging dependency sirf apne 2 slots kha sakti hai, poora process nahi.

Implementation mein ek simple counter `active` hai. `execute()` mein check `this.active < this.maxConcurrent` aur `this.active++` ek hi synchronous block mein hote hain -- beech mein koi `await` nahi -- isliye do calls ek hi slot nahi le sakte. Single thread yahan help karta hai: lock ki zaroorat nahi, bas check aur update ke beech await nahi hona chahiye.
why_needed: Interview mein log sochte hain Node mein concurrency limit ka matlab nahi. Asal mein Node ka strength hi bahut saare concurrent I/O calls hain, aur wahi weakness ban jaata hai jab ek dependency hang kare.
real_world_analogy: Ship ke watertight compartments (bulkhead naam wahi se aaya, code comment bhi yahi kehta hai): ek compartment mein paani aaye toh sirf woh doobta hai, poora jahaz nahi.
how_it_works: `active` counter in-flight calls ginta hai. Naya call: slot free hai toh `active++` aur chalao; nahi toh queue mein jagah hai toh `waitForSlot()`; nahi toh event `bulkhead-rejected` emit karke `BulkheadRejectedError` throw. Call khatam hone par `finally { this.release() }` slot chhodta (ya aage deta) hai.
in_this_project: `src/bulkhead.ts` mein `Bulkhead.execute`. `test/http.test.ts` ka test 'bulkhead: a server that hangs can hold at most 2 sockets' ek real loopback server ke saamne 6 calls bhejta hai jo hang karta hai: 2 server tak pahunchte hain aur 1500 ms TimeoutPolicy se (pehle 300 ms tha; busy machine par flaky tha, isliye widen kiya) `TimeoutError` paate hain, 4 turant `BulkheadRejectedError` paate hain, aur `s.hits()` 2 hota hai. `running` aur `queued` getters metrics ke liye hain.

Rejection turant aur sasta hai: operation chalta hi nahi
Lock ki zaroorat nahi, synchronous check-and-increment kaafi hai
disadvantages: Limit sirf ek process ke andar hai: 3 replicas = 3 x maxConcurrent
Sahi `maxConcurrent` value guess karni padti hai; adaptive limit implement nahi hai

Check aur `active++` ke beech `await` daal dena
Har call pe naya Bulkhead banana -- tab limit kabhi lagti hi nahi

question: In the bulkhead, why does a finishing call hand its slot directly to the oldest waiter instead of just decrementing the running count?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki 'pehle slot chhodo, phir waiter jaag ke le lega' ke beech ek gap hai, aur us gap mein koi naya call (newcomer) slot chheen sakta hai. Isko barging kehte hain: jo queue mein wait kar raha tha woh peeche reh gaya, aur jo abhi aaya woh aage nikal gaya. FIFO ka promise toot jaata hai, aur heavy load mein ek waiter baar baar starve ho sakta hai.

Gap kahan se aata hai? Waiter ek promise pe `await` kar raha hai. Jab release hota hai aur waiter ka promise resolve hota hai, uska continuation turant nahi chalta -- woh microtask queue mein jaata hai. Us beech mein koi aur microtask ya reaction chal sakta hai jo `execute()` call kare. Agar `active` pehle hi gir gaya hota, toh newcomer ko `active < maxConcurrent` true dikhta aur woh slot le leta.

Is project ka `release()` isliye counter ko chhuta hi nahi jab koi waiter hai: `this.queue.shift()` se sabse purana waiter nikalta hai, uska abort listener hatata hai, aur `next.resolve()` karta hai -- comment kehta hai 'the slot passes to the waiter; active stays the same'. Waiter jab jaagta hai toh slot pehle se uska hai; `waitForSlot` ka comment bhi yahi kehta hai 'resolves with the slot already ours'. `active` sirf tab ghatta hai jab queue khaali ho.

Isko test 'no barging' prove karta hai, aur mutation K4 ('release frees the slot, the waiter re-takes it later') ussi ek test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Fairness aur predictable latency: queue mein jo pehle aaya woh pehle chale. Bina hand-off ke FIFO queue sirf naam ki FIFO hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank counter pe token system: clerk free hua toh agla token number khud bulata hai. Agar clerk bas 'main free hoon' bol de aur log khud aayein, toh jo darwaze ke paas khada hai (newcomer) line wale se pehle pahunch jaayega.
how_it_works: `release()`: queue khaali -> `active--`. Queue mein koi -> `shift()` (oldest), `removeEventListener('abort', ...)`, `resolve()`. Running count release aur waiter ke start ke beech kabhi nahi girta, isliye beech mein aane wala `execute()` slot full dekhta hai aur queue mein peeche lagta hai (ya queue full ho toh reject).
in_this_project: `src/bulkhead.ts::release`. `test/bulkhead.test.ts` mein 'no barging: a newcomer arriving right after the slot is released goes behind the waiter' -- `maxConcurrent: 1, maxQueue: 1`, aur assertion `c.started` order `["a", "waiter", "newcomer"]`. README ke stage 2 mutation table mein K4 = 1 failed test. PLAN.md ka decision: 'the bulkhead hands a slot directly to the next waiter'.

question: Walk me through the 'no barging' test. How does it schedule a newcomer exactly in the gap between release and the waiter starting, without any timers?
answer_hinglish:
Test promise reaction order ka use karta hai. Setup: `Bulkhead({ maxConcurrent: 1, maxQueue: 1 })`. `pa = b.execute(op a)` -- slot le leta hai. `pw = b.execute(op waiter)` -- queue mein. Ab test `c.promise("a").then(() => { newcomer = b.execute(op newcomer) })` register karta hai.

Key point: bulkhead ke `execute` ne `return await operation(...)` mein a ke promise pe PEHLE reaction register kiya tha (jab a start hua). Test ka `.then` baad mein register hua. Jab test `c.finish("a").ok()` karta hai, promise a resolve hota hai aur uske reactions REGISTRATION ORDER mein chalte hain. Pehle bulkhead ka continuation: `finally` -> `release()` -> waiter ko hand-off (`next.resolve()`), lekin waiter ka continuation sirf microtask queue mein jaata hai, abhi chala nahi. Phir turant test ka reaction chalta hai -- yahi gap hai -- aur newcomer `execute()` call karta hai.

Sahi code mein `active` abhi bhi 1 hai, toh newcomer queue mein jaata hai (`b.queued` 1). Phir waiter ka continuation chalta hai aur waiter start hota hai. Assertion: `c.started` pehle `["a", "waiter"]`, phir waiter finish karo toh `["a", "waiter", "newcomer"]`.

K4 mutation mein release `active--` karta aur waiter jaag ke slot leta. Tab newcomer ko gap mein `active` 0 dikhta, woh turant start hota, aur started order galat ho jaata. Koi `setTimeout` nahi, koi sleep nahi -- isliye test deterministic hai, flaky nahi. `flush()` (setImmediate) sirf pending microtasks drain karne ke liye hai.
why_needed: Concurrency bugs timing se dikhte hain. Agar test random delays pe depend kare toh bug 'kabhi kabhi' pakda jaata hai. Reaction order se gap ko exact jagah pe hit karna test ko reliable banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Do log ek hi doorbell ke liye wait kar rahe hain: jo pehle bell pe kaan lagaye baitha hai (pehla registered listener) woh pehle react karega. Test ne jaan-boojh ke newcomer ko doosra listener banaya taaki woh exactly 'pehla react kar chuka, waiter abhi utha nahi' wale moment pe aaye.
how_it_works: Native promise ke `.then` reactions FIFO order mein microtasks bante hain. `await p` (native promise) bhi p pe directly reaction register karta hai. Bulkhead ka await a start hote hi register hua, test ka `.then` baad mein -- isliye bulkhead pehle. Waiter ka `await this.waitForSlot()` ek alag promise pe hai; uska resolve sirf naya microtask enqueue karta hai, jo test ke reaction ke BAAD chalta hai.
in_this_project: `test/bulkhead.test.ts` mein test ka comment khud explain karta hai: 'The bulkhead awaits a's promise first, so its release runs first; this reaction runs right after it, BEFORE the waiter's continuation.' Helper `controllable()` operations ko haath se finish karne deta hai aur `started` order record karta hai. README: K4 caught by 1 test (stage 2 aur stage 3 re-run dono mein 1).

question: A caller is waiting in the bulkhead's queue and its HTTP client disconnects. What happens, step by step?
answer_hinglish:
Waiter queue se nikal jaata hai, kabhi run nahi hota, aur caller ke reason ke saath reject hota hai. Uski queue wali jagah turant free ho jaati hai, toh koi naya call usko le sakta hai.

Step by step: `waitForSlot(signal)` ek promise banata hai aur agar signal diya gaya hai toh `waiter.onAbort` set karta hai, `signal.addEventListener("abort", waiter.onAbort, { once: true })`. Client disconnect hua -- Express adapter ka `requestSignal()` response ke `close` pe (agar response finish nahi hua) `ClientClosedError` ke saath abort karta hai. `onAbort` chalta hai: `this.queue.indexOf(waiter)`, `splice` se hatao, aur `reject(signal.reason)`. Execute mein `await this.waitForSlot()` throw karta hai -- aur yeh `try/finally` se PEHLE hai, isliye `release()` nahi chalta. Sahi bhi hai: waiter ne kabhi slot liya hi nahi tha, `active` usne badhaya nahi.

Ulta case bhi handle hai: agar waiter ko pehle slot mil gaya (hand-off), toh `release()` uska abort listener hata deta hai. Warna listener signal ki poori life tak pada rehta (K7 leak).

Aur beech ka case: slot hand-off ho gaya, lekin waiter ke jaagne se PEHLE caller abort kar de (listener already hat chuka). Pehle aisa waiter phir bhi apna operation chala deta tha, aborted signal ke saath -- yeh interview bank likhte waqt mila (README F5). Ab `execute()` jaagne ke baad `signal?.aborted` dobara check karta hai: aborted hai toh `release()` (slot agle waiter ko ya free) aur caller ka reason throw, operation nahi chalta. Test: 'a waiter aborted right after its slot was handed over does not run, and passes the slot on', mutation F5.

Aur agar caller PEHLE se aborted hai, `signal?.throwIfAborted()` sabse pehle line hai -- woh slot ya queue jagah leta hi nahi (mutation K8).

Kyun zaroori? Jo client chala gaya uske liye wait karna aur phir dependency ko call karna pure waste hai, aur ek real caller ki queue jagah bhi kha raha hai.
why_needed: Disconnect hue clients ka kaam karna load badhata hai bina kisi faayde ke. Queue bounded hai, toh mare hue waiters zinda waiters ki jagah block karte.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant waiting list: koi bina bataye chala gaya aur host ko pata chal gaya, toh uska naam list se kaat do -- table uske liye hold mat karo.
how_it_works: Abort listener `{ once: true }` ke saath. `onAbort`: indexOf + splice + reject. Hand-off pe `removeEventListener`. Rejection `waitForSlot` se aata hai, try block ke bahar, isliye `release()` (aur galat `active--`) nahi hota.
in_this_project: `src/bulkhead.ts::waitForSlot`. Tests: 'a queued caller that aborts leaves the queue, never runs, and its place is free' (`b.queued` 0 aur naya call 'b' us jagah aata hai), 'an already-aborted caller is refused before taking a slot', 'a waiter aborted right after its slot was handed over does not run, and passes the slot on' (F5). Mutations: K5 (aborted waiter stays in the queue) 1 test, K8 1 test. `src/adapters/express.ts::requestSignal` disconnect ko signal mein badalta hai.

question: What are breaker 'generations' and which three stale-result scenarios do they protect against?
answer_hinglish:
Generation ek counter hai jo har state change pe badhta hai (`transition()` mein `this.generation++`). Har call start hote waqt current generation yaad rakhta hai (`const generation = this.generation`), aur khatam hone par `record(generation, ...)` sirf tab kuch karta hai jab breaker abhi bhi ussi generation mein ho. Warna result 'stale' hai aur ignore.

Problem yeh hai ki calls async hain aur slow ho sakte hain. Ek call closed state mein shuru hua, 5 second laga, aur us beech breaker open ho gaya ya half-open bhi. Uska result 'dependency ab kaisi hai' ke baare mein kuch nahi batata. Teen cases, teeno tested:

1. Closed mein shuru hua, breaker open hone ke BAAD fail hua. Bina generation ke yeh failure open timer ko push back kar sakta (ya kuch bhi record karta). Test: open at t0, slow call t0+900 pe fail, t0+1000 pe breaker phir bhi half-open hai jaisa planned tha.
2. Closed mein shuru hua, half-open ke dauraan SUCCEED hua. Bina generation ke yeh probe gina jaata aur breaker close ho jaata bina kisi real probe ke. Test: state half-open hi rehti hai; phir real probe fail -> open.
3. Closed mein shuru hua, half-open ke dauraan FAIL hua. Bina generation ke yeh breaker reopen kar deta jabki real probe abhi chal raha hai. Test: state half-open rehti hai, real probe succeed -> closed.

README ke hisaab se mutation B9 ('no generation check') 2 tests ne pakda.
why_needed: Async world mein 'jab call shuru hua' aur 'jab result aaya' ke beech state badal sakti hai. Purane zamaane ka result naye zamaane ki state ko corrupt na kare -- yeh classic stale-write problem hai.
real_world_analogy: Election ke baad aaya postal vote: counting band ho chuki, naya round shuru. Woh vote purane round ka hai, naye round ke result mein nahi gina jaata.
how_it_works: `execute`: `const generation = this.generation` operation se pehle. `record()` ki pehli line: `if (generation !== this.generation) return;`. `transition()` har change pe generation++ karta hai, isliye closed->open, open->half-open, half-open->closed/open sab purane calls ko invalidate karte hain. Ek detail: refresh() bhi transition karta hai (open->half-open), toh woh bhi nayi generation hai.
in_this_project: `src/breaker.ts` mein `generation` field, `execute`, `record`, `transition`. `test/breaker.test.ts` ka describe 'CircuitBreaker: stale results (generations)' teen tests ke saath, helper `deferred()` se slow call haath se finish hota hai. README 'Generations' paragraph aur PLAN.md decision 'generations instead of trusting every late result'.

Teeno race conditions ek hi mechanism se band

Sirf half-open ke liye check lagana aur open timer wala case bhool jaana
Stale probe ka `probesInFlight--` karna -- naye half-open mein counter galat ho jaayega

Yeh idea DB mein kahan dikhta hai (optimistic locking, fencing tokens)?

question: How does the half-open state limit probes, and why is a finished probe's slot not reused?
answer_hinglish:
Half-open mein `halfOpenMaxCalls` (default 1) probes allowed hain, aur breaker close karne ke liye utne hi SUCCESSES chahiye. Check hai `this.probesInFlight + this.probeSuccesses >= this.halfOpenMaxCalls` -- true ho toh call ko `BrokenCircuitError { state: "half-open", retryAfterMs: 0 }` milta hai, operation chalta hi nahi.

Finished successful probe ka slot reuse kyun nahi? Kyunki formula mein `probeSuccesses` bhi gina jaata hai. Maan lo `halfOpenMaxCalls: 3`. 3 probes chal rahe hain. Ek succeed hua: `probesInFlight` 2, `probeSuccesses` 1, total 3 -- naya call phir bhi reject. Agar slot reuse hota, toh ek fast probe khatam hote hi naya probe aata, phir naya... aur half-open mein actual traffic 3 se zyada ho jaata. Half-open ka matlab hai 'recovering dependency pe sirf ek chhota controlled sample bhejo'. Total probes = exactly `halfOpenMaxCalls`, na kam na zyada.

Phir outcomes: koi bhi probe fail -> turant `transition("open")` (naya openMs, nayi generation, baaki in-flight probes stale ho jaate hain). Saare succeed -> `transition("closed")` with empty window. Aborted probe (caller gaya) -> sirf `probesInFlight--`, koi decision nahi, slot free.

Test 'halfOpenMaxCalls 3: needs 3 successful probes; the 4th concurrent call is rejected' yeh sab check karta hai, aur README mutation B7 ('a finished probe's slot is reused') 1 test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Recovering service fragile hoti hai. Half-open mein unlimited traffic bhejna usko phir gira sakta hai; probe count fix rakhna load ko bounded rakhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bridge repair ke baad: pehle 3 trucks bhejo test ke liye. Pehla truck paar ho gaya toh chauthe ko mat bhejo jab tak baaki 2 bhi paar na ho jaayein -- tabhi bridge public ke liye khulega.
how_it_works: `execute` half-open branch: limit check, phir `probesInFlight++`. `record` half-open branch: `probesInFlight--`; failure -> open; success -> `++probeSuccesses >= halfOpenMaxCalls` -> closed; ignored -> kuch nahi. `transition("half-open")` dono counters 0 karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/breaker.ts::probesInFlight` aur `probeSuccesses`. Tests: 'half-open: one probe goes through, a second concurrent call is rejected', 'halfOpenMaxCalls 3 ...', 'a probe whose caller aborted frees its slot without deciding anything', 'an error that is not a failure, in half-open, counts as a successful probe'. Mutations (final run): B6 (limit not enforced) 3, B7 1, B8 (failed probe does not reopen) 4, B14 (probe slot never freed) 1.

question: The breaker, bulkhead and retry budget all live in process memory. What does that mean when the API runs as three replicas?
answer_hinglish:
Har replica ke paas apna breaker, apna bulkhead, apna budget hoga -- teen independent copies. README 'NOT implemented' mein yeh seedha likha hai: 'Three API replicas have three of each (each replica learns on its own that a dependency is down).' Distributed state (jaise Redis mein shared breaker) PLAN mein 'Not in scope' hai.

Practical matlab:
1. Breaker: dependency down hui toh har replica ko khud `minimumCalls` (default 10) failures dekhne padenge open hone se pehle. 3 replicas = roughly 3 x itne failed calls dependency tak jaayenge. Aur load balancer traffic baantta hai, toh har replica ka window dheere bharta hai.
2. Bulkhead: `maxConcurrent: 20` ka matlab fleet level pe 60 concurrent calls. Agar dependency ne kaha 'max 30 concurrent', toh per-replica value 10 rakhni padegi -- aur autoscaling pe yeh math badal jaata hai.
3. Budget: har replica ka bucket alag drain hota hai. Outage mein har replica ke shuru ke kuch retries jaayenge (simulation mein per budget 3 extra attempts), phir har ek single attempt pe aa jaata hai.
4. Half-open probes: har replica apna probe bhejega, toh recovering dependency pe 3 probes aayenge.

Kya yeh bura hai? Hamesha nahi. Per-process state fast hai (bench mein breaker ~229-247 ns per call, koi network hop nahi), aur shared store ka failure (Redis down) breaker ko hi break nahi karta. Zyaadatar systems (resilience4j bhi default mein) per-instance state hi rakhte hain. Lekin limits fleet-level sochni padti hain, per-replica nahi.

real_world_analogy: Teen branches wala bank jahan har branch ka apna 'yeh customer fraud hai' register hai: ek branch ko pata chala toh baaki do ko khud seekhna padega.

question: What is a retry storm, and how does the RetryBudget turn 3000 attempts into 1003 in the project's simulation?
answer_hinglish:
Retry storm: dependency down hai, aur har client 3 attempts karta hai, toh dependency ko 3x traffic milta hai EXACTLY tab jab woh sabse kamzor hai. `budget.ts` ka comment yahi kehta hai, aur layers ho toh 3 x 3 x 3 = 27x. Recover hone ki koshish karti service pe yeh load usko phir gira deta hai.

`RetryBudget` gRPC ka retry throttling scheme hai: bucket `maxTokens` (default 10) se full shuru. Har failed attempt -1 token, har success +`tokenRatio` (default 0.1). Retry sirf tab allowed jab tokens > maxTokens / 2, yaani > 5. Ek budget per dependency, saare calls share karte hain.

Simulation (`budget.test.ts`, deterministic, koi timer nahi): 1000 calls, `maxAttempts: 3`, dependency hamesha down.
- Bina budget: 1000 x 3 = 3000 attempts.
- Budget ke saath: call 1 -- fail (9), retry, fail (8), retry, fail (7): 3 attempts. Call 2 -- fail (6) retry, fail (5): ab 5 half se UPAR nahi, toh give up: 2 attempts. Baaki 998 calls -- har ek fail karke token 0 tak jaata hai (never below 0), 1 attempt each. Total 3 + 2 + 998 = 1003.

Matlab outage mein extra load sirf 3 attempts ka tha; baaki system ek attempt per call pe aa gaya, jaise retries off ho gaye. Aur yeh automatic hai: koi 'outage detected' flag nahi, sirf success ratio. Real sockets pe bhi same shape: 20 calls closed port pe = 23 connection attempts (`http.test.ts`).

Note: budget retries ko kam karta hai, calls ko nahi -- har call phir bhi ek attempt karta hai. Calls band karna breaker ka kaam hai.
why_needed: Retry transient errors ke liye achha hai, sustained outage ke liye zehar. Budget dono cases ko bina config change ke alag handle karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Office mein sab log ek hi printer pe 'print' teen baar dabate hain jab woh jam hai -- jam aur bura. Rule: 'jab tak printer theek se chal raha hai tab tak dobara try karo, warna ek baar dabao aur jao.'
how_it_works: Tokens > max/2 ka check `canRetry()`. RetryPolicy mein order: shouldRetry (non-retryable ho toh budget untouched) -> `budget.onFailure()` -> maxAttempts check -> `canRetry()` check. Success pe `budget.onSuccess()`. Token min 0, max `maxTokens` pe clamp.

README table: no budget 3000, with `RetryBudget()` 1003. `test/http.test.ts` 'server down (connection refused) with a shared budget' -> 23. Mutations R13 (threshold inclusive) 4, R19 (budget not checked) 4.

question: How is the breaker's count-based sliding window implemented, and why is each update O(1)?
answer_hinglish:
Window ek ring buffer hai: `ring: boolean[]` jiska size `windowSize` (default 20) hai, `true` = failure. Saath mein teen numbers: `next` (agla likhne ka index), `count` (kitne slots bhare hain, max windowSize) aur `failures` (window mein kitne true). Failure rate = `failures / count`.

`record()` mein closed state ka naya outcome aata hai toh:
1. Agar window full hai (`count === windowSize`), toh `ring[next]` sabse purana outcome hai jo ab bahar jaayega -- agar woh failure tha toh `failures--`. Warna `count++`.
2. `ring[next] = failed`, aur failed ho toh `failures++`.
3. `next = (next + 1) % windowSize`.
4. Check: `count >= minimumCalls && failures / count >= threshold` -> open.

Har step constant time hai -- poora array kabhi scan nahi hota, kyunki `failures` running total hai jo aane-jaane wale outcome se adjust hota hai. Isliye har call pe cost window size se independent hai.

Close hone par (`transition("closed")`) `ring.fill(false)`, `next`, `count`, `failures` sab 0 -- empty window, purani failures bhool jaao (mutation B10 'window not reset on close' 1 test se pakda).

Dhyan do: window sirf CLOSED state mein bharta hai; open/half-open mein record() pehle hi return kar deta hai. Aur 'sliding' test: windowSize 4, threshold 0.75 -- [boom, boom, ok, ok] 2/4, phir [ok, ok] se dono failures bahar 0/4, phir boom boom 2/4 closed, ek aur boom 3/4 = 75% open. Mutation B1 'old failures never leave the window' isi test se pakda gaya.
why_needed: Breaker har call pe chalta hai, toh window update sasta hona chahiye. Ring buffer + running counter memory fixed aur time constant rakhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Cricket mein 'last 20 balls ka strike rate': naya ball aaya toh 21st purana ball list se nikal jaata hai. Har ball pe poori list dobara nahi ginte, bas jo gaya usko ghatao aur jo aaya usko jodo.
how_it_works: Fixed-size array + write pointer modulo size. Eviction implicit hai: overwrite se pehle purana value padh ke counter adjust. `count` alag rakha hai taaki window bharne se pehle (count < windowSize) rate sahi nikle aur `minimumCalls` check ho sake.

README overhead table (ek Windows PC, Node 20.20.1, no-op operation): circuit breaker 229 / 247 ns per call do runs mein. PLAN: 'count-based sliding window for the breaker (last N calls, ring buffer)'.

question: How does the breaker go from open to half-open without a timer?
answer_hinglish:
Lazily: koi `setTimeout` nahi chalta. Breaker sirf `openedAt` (open hone ka time) yaad rakhta hai. Jab bhi koi breaker ko 'dekhta' hai -- `execute()` ya `state` getter -- `refresh()` chalta hai: agar state open hai aur `now() - openedAt >= openMs`, toh `transition("half-open")`. Matlab open->half-open ka transition agle call pe hota hai, ghadi pe nahi.

Kyun? PLAN.md ka decision: 'Nothing runs in the background, and an idle breaker costs nothing.' Timer approach mein har breaker ka ek timer hota jo process ko zinda rakh sakta hai (tests mein 'timer left' problems), cleanup karna padta, aur jis breaker pe koi traffic hi nahi uske liye bhi kaam hota. Lazy check ek subtraction hai.

Iska ek side effect: open state mein `retryAfterMs` bhi isi se nikalta hai -- `Math.max(0, openedAt + openMs - now())`. Test: open hone ke 400 ms baad call karo (openMs 1000) toh `retryAfterMs` 600 milta hai, aur operation 0 baar call hota hai.

Test 'after openMs it is half-open (checked lazily, no timer)': 999 ms advance -> abhi open; 1 ms aur -> half-open, aur `onStateChange` ko `{ from: "open", to: "half-open" }` milta hai. Time test hook `now` se control hota hai, fake timers ki zaroorat nahi.

Ek baat yaad rakho: `state` getter read karna bhi transition (aur event) trigger kar sakta hai -- yeh pure read nahi hai.
why_needed: Background timers resource leak, test flakiness aur cleanup bugs laate hain. Lazy evaluation same behaviour deta hai bina in problems ke.
real_world_analogy: Parking meter jo khud bell nahi bajata; jab warden aata hai tab dekhta hai 'time khatam hua kya'. Koi nahi aaya toh kuch hone ki zaroorat bhi nahi.
how_it_works: `openedAt = now()` `transition("open")` mein set hota hai. `refresh()`: `if (current === "open" && now() - openedAt >= openMs) transition("half-open")`. `>=` hai, isliye exactly openMs pe half-open. Probe failure pe naya `openedAt` (B15 'reopen keeps the old open time' 4 tests in the final run).
in_this_project: `src/breaker.ts::refresh`, `execute` aur `state` getter dono isko call karte hain. `now` option ek test hook hai (default `Date.now`). Test 'defaults: window 20, minimum 10, 50%, 30 s' mein 29 999 ms pe open, 30 000 pe half-open. Mutation B5 ('never goes half-open') final run mein 14 tests ne pakda (stage 2 mein 12; hanging-probe aur throwing-isFailure tests bhi ab ise pakadte hain).

Idle breaker zero cost

question: Why does RetryBudget count tokens in thousandths, and why does the failing attempt pay before the canRetry() check?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag decisions hain.

1. Thousandths: `SCALE = 1000`. `maxTokens` 10 andar 10000 hai, `tokenRatio` 0.1 andar 100. Saari arithmetic integers mein, toh floating point drift nahi. Float mein 50 x 0.1 = 5.000000000000002 aata hai (test comment yahi likhta hai), aur threshold check `tokens > max / 2` hai -- 5.000000000000002 > 5 true ho jaata, jabki exactly 5 pe retry band hona chahiye. Integers mein 50 x 100 = 5000, exact. gRPC bhi thousandths use karta hai. Side effect: `tokenRatio` max 3 decimals; 0.0001 round hoke 0 hota hai aur constructor `RangeError` deta hai (tested).

2. Failure pehle charge: RetryPolicy mein order hai `budget.onFailure()` -> `maxAttempts` check -> `budget.canRetry()`. Matlab jo attempt abhi fail hua uska token pehle katega, phir decide hoga retry karna hai ya nahi. Consequence: retry ke liye tokens > threshold + 1 hone chahiye jab failure aaye. README: 'right after canRetry() turns true again, the next single failure is still not retried.'

Kyun yeh order? Failure ek real signal hai dependency ki health ka -- usko account na karna galat hoga. Aur outage simulation ka 1003 isi order se aata hai: call 2 pe fail (6) -> retry, fail (5) -> stop.

Tests: '50 x 0.1 is exactly 5', '1000 x 0.001 is exactly 1', aur recovery test jisme 5.1 tokens pe blip retry NAHI hota (5.1 - 1 = 4.1), lekin 6.2 pe hota hai (5.2 > 5).
why_needed: Threshold-based logic floats ke saath edge pe galat decision leta hai. Aur budget ka order decide karta hai ki outage mein exactly kitne extra attempts jaate hain.
real_world_analogy: Paise ko paise mein nahi, paise mein ginte ho (Rs 10.10 ko 1010 paise) taaki rounding kabhi galat total na de. Aur bill pehle katta hai, phir dekhte ho balance mein agla order ka paisa hai ya nahi.
how_it_works: `this.max = Math.round(maxTokens * SCALE)`, `this.ratio = Math.round(tokenRatio * SCALE)`. `onSuccess`: `min(max, tokens + ratio)`. `onFailure`: `max(0, tokens - SCALE)`. `canRetry`: `tokens > max / 2` (strict). `available` getter `tokens / SCALE` return karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/budget.ts::SCALE`, `RetryBudget`; `src/retry.ts` mein order. `test/budget.test.ts` 'no drift' aur 'retries come back by themselves once the dependency recovers'. Mutations: R13 (threshold inclusive) 4, R14 (refill not capped) 1, R15 (goes negative) 2.
advantages: Exact arithmetic, threshold edge pe bhi deterministic
gRPC ke behaviour se match
Failure ka signal kabhi miss nahi hota
disadvantages: tokenRatio 3 decimals tak limited
Recovery ke baad retries thoda der se wapas aate hain (extra 1 token ki wajah se)
common_mistakes: Budget ko float mein rakhna aur `>=` use karna
canRetry pehle check karna aur failure baad mein charge -- extra retry milega
Non-retryable error ka bhi token kaatna
follow_up_questions: Agar order ulta karo (check pehle, charge baad mein) toh 1000-call simulation mein kitne attempts honge?
Max 0 ya negative tokenRatio kyun reject?
BigInt ki zaroorat kabhi padegi?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Integer fixed-point vs float: integers exact hain lekin precision fix (0.001). Is use case ke liye kaafi hai. Charge-before-check conservative hai: recovery pe retries thoda late, lekin outage mein extra load kam.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi refactor charge ko check ke baad le jaaye toh har call ko ek extra retry milega threshold ke aas paas -- simulation ka 1003 badal jaayega aur test fail hoga (yahi us test ka value hai).
advanced.alternatives: Token bucket by time (rate-based), AIMD style adaptive retry, ya client-side 'retry ratio' (jaise kuch libraries: retries <= 10% of requests). Budget success-ratio based hai, time-based nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale se arithmetic nahi badalta; per-call do integer ops. Zyada traffic pe bucket fast drain/refill hota hai, behaviour ratio-based rehta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: `available` ko gauge ke roop mein export karo; `tokenRatio` ko dependency ke normal error rate ke hisaab se tune karo (0.1 ka matlab roughly: har 10 successes ek failure 'afford' ho sakta hai).

question: The breaker's isFailure returns false for a 404. Why does the project count that call as a SUCCESS instead of ignoring it?
answer_hinglish:
`isFailure(error)` ka sawaal hai: 'kya yeh error batata hai ki dependency UNHEALTHY hai?' 404, validation error -- dependency ne sahi jawab diya, bas jawab 'nahi mila' tha. Toh woh health window mein SUCCESS gina jaata hai: `isFailure(error) ? "failure" : "success"`. Error phir bhi caller ko rethrow hota hai -- breaker sirf apni bookkeeping badalta hai, result nahi.

Ignore kyun nahi? PLAN.md ka reason: 'a service answering 404 to everything is healthy, and ignoring those calls would let a few 5xx decide alone.' Example: 100 calls, 95 ka jawab 404, 5 ka 503. Agar 404 ignore karo toh window mein sirf 5 entries, sab failure -- 100% failure rate (minimumCalls poora hone par) aur breaker open, jabki service 95% time sahi jawab de rahi thi. Success ginne se rate 5% aata hai, jo sach hai.

Default `isFailure` har error ko failure maanta hai. Real use mein `isFailure: isRetryableHttp` do -- woh network errors, timeouts, 408, 429, 5xx (501 chhod ke) ko failure, baaki 4xx ko non-failure maanta hai. README usage example mein yahi hai: 'a 404 is not "down"'.

Half-open mein bhi same: non-failure error ek successful probe hai (test 'an error that is not a failure, in half-open, counts as a successful probe' -> closed).

Ek edge jo interview bank likhte waqt mila (README F3): agar user ka `isFailure` khud THROW kare, toh pehle `record()` chalta hi nahi tha -- half-open probe apna slot kabhi release nahi karta aur breaker half-open mein atak jaata, har call reject. Ab `classify()` throwing isFailure ko failure maanta hai; test 'an isFailure that throws counts as a failure; in half-open it does not leave the breaker stuck', mutation F3.

Mutations: B12 'isFailure ignored' 3 tests, B13 'non-failures ignored instead of counted as success' 1 test -- B13 exactly yahi design decision check karta hai.
why_needed: Galat classification se breaker ya toh healthy service ko kaat deta hai (false open) ya ek chhote sample se decide karta hai. Dono production incidents hain.
real_world_analogy: Doctor se 'kya aapke paas yeh dawai hai?' poocha, jawab 'nahi'. Doctor bimaar nahi hai -- usne sahi jawab diya. Usko 'unavailable' list mein daalna galat hoga.
how_it_works: Catch block mein: caller aborted -> 'ignored'; warna `classify(error)`: `isFailure(error)` true -> 'failure', false -> 'success', throw kare -> 'failure'. 'success' window mein `false` likhta hai, `failures` nahi badhta, `count` badhta hai.
in_this_project: `src/breaker.ts` `execute` ka catch block aur option `isFailure`. `src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp` doosra role bhi nibhata hai. Tests: 'errors that are not failures count as successes (the dependency answered)' -- 10 x 404, state closed, failureRate 0; `test/http.test.ts` '404s do not open a breaker that uses isRetryableHttp as isFailure' -- 10 real 404s, closed, server ne 10 hits dekhe.

Ek function (`isRetryableHttp`) retry aur breaker dono ke liye consistent

disadvantages: Default 'every error' naive hai -- user ko `isFailure` dena yaad rakhna padta hai
Business errors jo actually dependency bug hain (galat 400) bhi healthy gine jaayenge

question: The breaker is half-open and its single probe never finishes. What happens, and how does the project tell you to prevent it?
answer_hinglish:
Breaker hamesha ke liye half-open mein phas jaata hai. Probe ne slot le liya (`probesInFlight` 1), `halfOpenMaxCalls` 1 hai, toh har naya call `BrokenCircuitError { state: "half-open", retryAfterMs: 0 }` paata hai. Probe ka result kabhi nahi aata, toh `record()` kabhi nahi chalta: na close, na reopen, aur koi timer bhi nahi jo bachaye (transitions lazy hain). Dependency theek ho jaaye tab bhi traffic band rahega.

README seedha kehta hai: 'A probe that never finishes keeps its slot forever: put a TimeoutPolicy inside the breaker.' Recommended order retry -> breaker -> bulkhead -> timeout mein timeout breaker ke ANDAR hai. Toh hanging probe ko TimeoutPolicy abort karta hai aur `TimeoutError` se reject karta hai; breaker usko failure maanta hai (isRetryableHttp TimeoutError ko retryable/failure kehta hai), `transition("open")`, naya openMs, aur kuch der baad naya probe.

Note: caller ka abort bhi slot free karta hai -- agar probe ka caller (jaise HTTP client) disconnect kare, toh outcome 'ignored', `probesInFlight--`, slot free, koi decision nahi. Lekin yeh bharosa karne layak nahi: background job ka caller kabhi abort nahi karega.

Yahi baat slow calls ke liye bhi: breaker mein slow-call rate nahi hai (README NOT implemented), toh slow calls ko failure banane ka tareeka bhi andar wala timeout hi hai.
why_needed: Breaker ka poora recovery path probe ke result pe tika hai. Result na aaye toh recovery kabhi nahi hoti -- silent, permanent outage.
real_world_analogy: Toll booth pe ek test car bheji 'bridge theek hai kya?' aur woh kabhi wapas nahi aayi na koi khabar. Jab tak koi deadline nahi, booth hamesha band rahega.
how_it_works: Half-open limit check `probesInFlight + probeSuccesses >= halfOpenMaxCalls`. Slot sirf `record()` mein free hota hai (success/failure/ignored). Andar ka TimeoutPolicy `Promise.race` se ms ke baad reject karta hai aur operation ka signal abort karta hai, toh record() guaranteed chalta hai.
in_this_project: README CircuitBreaker section ki last bullet aur 'Composition: why this order'. `src/wrap.ts` ka comment order samjhaata hai. `src/timeout.ts::TimeoutPolicy`. Ab iska dedicated test hai (pehle sirf reasoning thi; review ke baad add hua): `test/wrap.test.ts` 'a half-open probe that hangs blocks the breaker forever; a timeout INSIDE the breaker turns it into a failure' -- bina timeout ke state half-open atka rehta hai, timeout andar ho toh open (naya openMs). Related: 'a probe whose caller aborted frees its slot without deciding anything' aur mutation B14 ('probe slot never freed') 1 test.

question: A dependency starts hanging and six requests hit it at once through a bulkhead of 2. What do the six callers see?
answer_hinglish:
Do callers ko `TimeoutError` milta hai aur chaar ko turant `BulkheadRejectedError`. Yahi `test/http.test.ts` ka real test hai: ek loopback `node:http` server jo kabhi jawab nahi deta, `Bulkhead({ maxConcurrent: 2 })` (default `maxQueue` 0) aur har call ke andar `TimeoutPolicy({ ms: 1500 })` (pehle 300 ms tha; 100% CPU par dono requests server tak time par nahi pahunchti thin, toh widen kiya). 6 calls ek saath. Results: 4 `BulkheadRejectedError`, 2 `TimeoutError`, aur server ne sirf 2 hits dekhe.

Kyun yeh achha hai? Bina bulkhead ke saare 6 (ya 600) requests socket khol ke 1500 ms (ya poora default timeout) tak latakte. Process ke sockets, memory, aur event loop pe kaam badhta. Bulkhead ke saath hanging dependency 'sirf apne slots' kha sakti hai. Rejected callers ko turant pata chal jaata hai, aur Express adapter usko 503 + `Retry-After: 1` mein badal deta hai (`mapResilienceError`), toh client ko clear signal milta hai.

Timeout bhi zaroori hai: bina timeout ke woh 2 slots hamesha ke liye pakde rahenge aur bulkhead permanently full -- har naya call reject. Isliye timeout bulkhead ke andar.

Agar `maxQueue` > 0 hota, toh extra calls queue mein wait karte aur slot free hone par (timeout ke baad) chalte -- lekin unka bhi wahi hashr hota agar dependency abhi bhi hang hai.
why_needed: Ek dependency ka hang poore service ka outage na bane -- failure ko contain karna bulkhead ka poora point hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter wala chai stall jahan 2 log hi line mein khade ho sakte hain. Chaiwala gayab hai; 2 log wait karke thak ke jaate hain, baaki 4 ko door se hi 'abhi nahi' sunai deta hai -- woh kahin aur chale jaate hain.
how_it_works: Pehle 2 calls `active++`, baaki 4 ke liye `active` 2 hai aur queue length 0 = maxQueue, toh reject branch. 1500 ms baad TimeoutPolicy operation ka signal abort karta hai (fetch cancel, server connection close dekhta hai) aur reject karta hai; bulkhead ka `finally` slot release karta hai.
in_this_project: Test 'bulkhead: a server that hangs can hold at most 2 sockets; the rest are refused at once' `test/http.test.ts` mein. README 'What each policy does' -> Bulkhead: 'tested over HTTP: 6 calls to a hanging server, 2 reach it and time out, 4 are refused at once'. Adapter mapping `src/adapters/http-status.ts::mapResilienceError`.

question: A client disconnects while its call is running through the breaker. Why is that call not recorded, and what would go wrong if it were?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki caller ka abort dependency ke baare mein kuch nahi batata. Code: catch mein `signal?.aborted ? "ignored" : ...`. Ignored outcome closed state mein window ko chhuta hi nahi, aur half-open mein sirf `probesInFlight--` karta hai -- slot free, koi decision nahi.

Agar record hota toh kya bigadta? Socho ek mobile app ke users network badalne pe disconnect karte hain, ya load balancer ka idle timeout. Har disconnect `requestSignal` ko abort karta hai, aur operation (fetch) `AbortError` ke saath fail hota hai. Agar yeh failures gine jaate, toh 'clients jaldi chale gaye' wala pattern breaker ko open kar deta -- healthy dependency kaat di jaati, aur BAAKI users ko 503 milta. Ek client-side problem server-side outage ban jaata. Half-open mein aur bura: ek aborted probe breaker ko phir open kar deta.

Doosri taraf, ek aborted call ko success ginna bhi galat hoga -- hume pata hi nahi dependency ne kya kiya. Isliye teesra outcome 'ignored'.

Already-aborted caller ka case alag hai: `signal?.throwIfAborted()` execute ki pehli line hai, operation chalta hi nahi aur kuch record nahi hota (test 'an already-aborted caller: not called, not recorded', mutation B18).

Tests: 'a call whose caller aborted is not recorded' -- 10 aborted calls, state closed, failureRate 0; 'a probe whose caller aborted frees its slot without deciding anything' -- state half-open rehti hai, agla call probe ban ke close karta hai. Mutation B11 ('calls of aborted callers recorded') 2 tests.
why_needed: Breaker ka signal saaf hona chahiye. Client behaviour (disconnects) ko dependency health samajhna false opens ka classic source hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant ka customer order dekar chala gaya; kitchen ne khana banaya ya nahi, pata nahi. Kitchen ko 'fail' mark karna galat, 'pass' mark karna bhi galat -- us order ko rating mein ginte hi nahi.
how_it_works: Teen-valued outcome: success / failure / ignored. Aborted check sirf catch path mein hai: agar operation abort ke bawajood SUCCESS de de, toh woh success record hota hai (dependency ne sach mein jawab diya). Generation check pehle hota hai, toh stale aborted calls kuch nahi karte.
in_this_project: `src/breaker.ts` `execute` catch aur `record` ka 'ignored' branch. Abort source production mein `src/adapters/express.ts::requestSignal` ya Nest ka `@RequestSignal()` hota hai. Tests `test/breaker.test.ts` mein. README: 'A call whose caller aborted is not recorded at all; an aborted probe frees its slot without deciding anything.'

Aborted probe deadlock nahi banata
Success-despite-abort sahi information ke roop mein record hota hai
disadvantages: Agar dependency ki slowness hi disconnects ka kaaran hai (client thak ke gaya), woh signal kho jaata hai -- isliye andar timeout chahiye jo caller se chhota ho
Teen-valued outcome code ko thoda complex banata hai
common_mistakes: Har error ko failure ginna, AbortError bhi
Aborted probe pe slot free na karna
Sochna ki caller ka abort aur TimeoutPolicy ka abort same hain -- timeout ka abort andar ka signal hai, caller ka nahi, aur woh failure gina jaata hai
follow_up_questions: TimeoutPolicy ka abort breaker ke liye 'ignored' kyun nahi hai?
Agar saare clients 1 s pe disconnect karein aur dependency 2 s leti ho toh breaker kya dekhega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ignore karna dependency ki slowness ka ek signal kho deta hai. Trade-off isliye theek hai kyunki slowness ko capture karne ka sahi tool andar ka TimeoutPolicy hai, jiska timeout caller ke patience se chhota hona chahiye.

advanced.alternatives: Aborted calls ko alag 'slow' bucket mein ginna, ya slow-call rate threshold (resilience4j style) -- dono is project mein implement nahi hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic pe disconnect rate absolute terms mein badhta hai; agar recorded hota toh false opens 10x-100x zyada common hote. Ignore rule scale pe aur valuable hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Ignored calls ka counter metric (abhi nahi hai) aur caller-abort vs timeout ka ratio dashboard pe -- isse pata chalega timeouts sahi tune hain ya nahi.

question: A dependency was down long enough to drain the retry budget, and now it has recovered. How quickly do retries come back, and how do the breaker and budget interact during recovery?
answer_hinglish:
Budget ke numbers README mein measured hain (deterministic simulation, `budget.test.ts`): 100 failing calls ne bucket 0 kar diya. Recovery ke baad 51 successes = 5.1 tokens, aur `canRetry()` true ho jaata hai (5.1 > 5). LEKIN agla single failure abhi bhi retry nahi hota: failing attempt pehle token kaat-ta hai, 5.1 - 1 = 4.1, check fail. Total 72 successes (51 + 21 = 6.2 tokens) ke baad ek blip retry hota hai: 6.2 - 1 = 5.2 > 5. Toh default settings pe retries 'wapas' aane ke liye ~72 successful calls chahiye.

Breaker ke saath interaction (recommended order retry -> breaker -> ...): jab breaker open hai, calls `BrokenCircuitError` paate hain. `isRetryableHttp` usko non-retryable kehta hai, aur non-retryable errors budget ko chhoote nahi -- toh open breaker na budget drain karta hai na refill. Refill sirf real successes se hota hai, jo breaker close hone ke baad aate hain. Sequence: dependency down -> retries budget drain karte hain, failures window bharte hain -> breaker open (calls band) -> openMs baad probe -> success -> closed, empty window -> successes budget refill karte hain -> ~72 successes baad retries normal.

Kya yeh slow hai? Intentionally conservative hai: recovery ke turant baad dependency fragile hoti hai, aur early retries usko phir gira sakte hain. Low-traffic service pe 72 calls minutes le sakte hain -- tab tak blips retry nahi honge. Agar yeh unacceptable ho toh `tokenRatio` badhao (faster refill) -- trade-off outage mein thoda zyada extra load.

Yeh poora interaction ek integrated test mein nahi hai; budget recovery aur breaker recovery alag alag tested hain.
why_needed: Senior interview mein 'outage ke baad kya hota hai' utna hi important hai jitna 'outage mein kya hota hai'. Recovery dynamics galat ho toh service oscillate karti hai.
real_world_analogy: Injury ke baad cricketer: fitness test pass (probe) karke team mein wapas, lekin pehle kuch matches mein usko full overs nahi dete jab tak form (tokens) wapas na aaye.
how_it_works: Budget: success +0.1, failure -1, retry only if > 5 AFTER charging the failure. Breaker: probe success -> closed with empty window. Retry ke andar breaker hai, toh BrokenCircuitError retry loop tak aata hai aur `shouldRetry: isRetryableHttp` usko 'not-retryable' bana deta hai -- budget untouched (`retry.ts` mein shouldRetry check onFailure se pehle).
in_this_project: `test/budget.test.ts` 'retries come back by themselves once the dependency recovers' (51, blip not retried, +21 -> 6.2, blip retried). README: 'After recovery, 51 successes make canRetry() true again, and 72 in total make a single failure retried again.' `src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp` breaker rejection ko false deta hai; `test/wrap.test.ts` 'an open breaker inside retry (with isRetryableHttp) stops the retry at once'.
advantages: Recovery ke baad gradual ramp: fragile dependency pe extra load nahi
Open breaker budget ko distort nahi karta (non-retryable)
Sab automatic, koi manual reset nahi
disadvantages: Low traffic pe retries ghanton tak 'off' reh sakte hain
Per-process: har replica alag refill hota hai
Integrated breaker+budget recovery ka test nahi hai
common_mistakes: Breaker ko retry ke bahar rakhna -- tab budget aur breaker dono ka signal bigadta hai
Sochna ki canRetry() true = agla failure retry hoga
Recovery ke baad budget manually reset karna -- storm wapas
follow_up_questions: tokenRatio 0.5 karo toh recovery aur outage dono kaise badlenge?
Budget ko time ke saath bhi refill karna chahiye?
Breaker close hote hi traffic spike kaise handle karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Conservative recovery (charge-before-check, slow refill) vs fast recovery. Is project ne conservative chuna. Faster refill ka cost: agla outage start hone par zyada retries jaayenge pehle budget drain ho.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Flapping dependency (30 s up, 30 s down): budget kabhi refill hi nahi hota, retries permanently off -- jo shayad sahi hai. Breaker open/close oscillate karega; har close ke baad window empty hai toh minimumCalls failures ke baad phir open.
advanced.alternatives: Time-based refill (tokens per second), budget reset on breaker close, ya adaptive concurrency (Netflix concurrency-limits style). Inme se kuch implement nahi hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x traffic: 72 successes jaldi aate hain, recovery fast. 100x replicas: har replica ko apne 72 chahiye, lekin har ek ko traffic ka 1/100 milta hai -- recovery slow ho sakti hai. Yeh per-process state ki hidden cost hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Dashboard pe budget `available`, breaker state, aur give-up reasons ek saath; alert jab budget 'budget' give-ups dependency recovery ke X minute baad bhi chal rahe hon. tokenRatio ko traffic profile ke hisaab se per dependency tune karo.

question: In the stage 2 mutation run one break survived: K7. What was it, why did no test catch it, and how was it fixed?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: stage 2 mein 27 deliberate breaks lagaye, 26 pakde gaye. K7 survive kiya: 'abort listener not removed on hand-off'. Matlab jab queued waiter ko slot milta hai, `release()` uska `abort` listener caller ke signal se nahi hatata. Poori test suite green rahi.

Investigation: K7 kya bigadta hai? Listener `{ once: true }` ke saath hai aur `onAbort` mein `indexOf` -1 aata hai kyunki waiter already queue se shift ho chuka. Toh agar baad mein abort ho bhi jaaye, `reject()` ek already-resolved promise pe chalta hai -- no-op. Koi visible behaviour change nahi: result same, order same, counts same. Isliye koi assertion fail nahi hua. README ke shabdon mein: 'a leak with no visible effect'.

Cause: leak hai. Ek long-lived signal (jaise ek worker ka shutdown signal jo har job ko pass hota hai) pe har queued call ek closure chhodta jaayega jo waiter aur bulkhead ko pakde rakhta hai. Memory dheere dheere badhti hai, aur Node 'MaxListenersExceededWarning' de sakta hai.

Fix: ek test add kiya jo signal ke `addEventListener` aur `removeEventListener` ko spy karta hai, aur assert karta hai `removed` == `added` hand-off ke baad. Ab K7 ek test se pakda jaata hai (stage 3 re-run mein bhi 1). Suite 129 se 130 tests.

Lesson: 'tests pass' ka matlab 'behaviour sahi' hai, 'resources sahi' nahi. Leaks ke liye directly resource count karo -- listeners, timers (timeout tests bhi 'no timer left' check karte hain).
why_needed: Mutation testing ka asli value survivors mein hai: woh batate hain test suite kahan andha hai. Interview mein 'meri ek test gap kaise mili' ek strong story hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar se nikalte waqt gas band karna bhool gaye, lekin burner already bujha hua tha -- aaj kuch nahi hua. Check karne ka tareeka: 'kya khana bana' nahi, 'kya knob band hai' dekhna.
how_it_works: Spy: signal ke methods ko wrap karke har call record karo, phir original call karo. Hand-off ke baad `removed` array `added` ke barabar hona chahiye. Mutation runner har break ko akela lagata, poori suite chalata, revert karta hai.
in_this_project: Fix `src/bulkhead.ts::release` mein ek line hai: `if (next.onAbort !== undefined) next.signal!.removeEventListener("abort", next.onAbort);`. Test: `test/bulkhead.test.ts` 'a waiter that gets its slot removes its abort listener from the caller's signal (no leak)'. README 'Stage 2 ... The survivor was K7 ... A test that spies on the signal's listeners was added; K7 is now caught.'

Test cheap hai, koi heap snapshot nahi

Sirf behaviour assert karna, resources nahi

question: The first stage 2 mutation run gave unstable counts: the same break failed 1 test, then 6. How was that tracked down?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: same mutation, do runs, alag failed counts -- 1, phir 6. Mutation testing ka poora matlab hi deterministic count hai, toh yeh red flag tha.

Investigation: extra failures ke NAAM padhe. Sab ek jaise the: 'expected BulkheadRejectedError to be an instance of BulkheadRejectedError'. Yeh absurd lagta hai -- same naam ki class ka instance nahi? Matlab do ALAG class objects the jinka naam same tha. Yaani error classes ka module do baar load hua tha: ek copy ne error throw kiya, doosri copy ke against `instanceof` check hua, aur prototype chain match nahi hui.

Cause: runner vitest ko lowercase drive path (`h:\...`) se start kar raha tha. Windows pe paths case-insensitive hain, lekin module cache path string pe key hota hai -- `h:\project\...\errors.ts` aur `H:\project\...\errors.ts` do alag modules ban gaye. Uppercase `H:\` se same breaks ne 3 mein se 3 runs mein same counts diye, aur clean suite kabhi fail nahi hua (8 of 8 runs).

Fix: runs `H:\` se chalaye; stage 2 numbers aur stage 1 re-run unhi se hain. Stage 1 wala original table lowercase run se tha, isliye README kehta hai re-run hi trust karo. B1 parking lot project ke commit mein bhi yahi artefact 13 counts inflate kar raha tha.

Lesson README se: 'a noisy mutation count can make a break look caught when it is not -- check unexpected failures by name.' Kyunki agar break ko sirf duplicate-module artefact pakad raha hai, toh woh actually survivor hai.

Code impact bhi samjho: `isRetryableHttp` `instanceof BrokenCircuitError` use karta hai. Agar production bundle mein library do baar load ho (do versions), wahi bug real ho jaayega.
why_needed: Flaky tooling se galat confidence aata hai. Interview mein debugging story jisme 'error message dhyan se padha' aur root cause environment nikla -- yeh senior signal hai.
real_world_analogy: Do photocopy ek hi form ki, alag machine se -- dikhne mein same, lekin stamp match nahi karta kyunki office sirf original pe lage stamp ko maanta hai.
how_it_works: JS `instanceof` prototype chain mein `Class.prototype` object identity check karta hai. Module do baar evaluate hua = do class objects = do prototypes. ESM loader module ko resolved URL/path se cache karta hai; case alag = key alag.
in_this_project: `src/errors.ts::BulkheadRejectedError` aur `src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp` (instanceof based). README section 'A test-environment finding.' Fix code mein nahi, test environment (run from `H:\`) mein. Mutation runner repo ke bahar rakha gaya.
advantages: Root cause error message se mila, guess se nahi
Numbers ko trust karne se pehle repeatability check (3/3, 8/8)
README honestly batata hai kaunsa table kis run se hai
disadvantages: Fix environment discipline pe depend karta hai (uppercase path), code pe nahi
Same issue production mein duplicate package versions se aa sakta hai -- library usko handle nahi karti
common_mistakes: Unstable counts ko 'average' le lena
Failures ke naam na padhna, sirf count dekhna
Sochna Windows path case kabhi matter nahi karta
follow_up_questions: `instanceof` ki jagah `error.name` check karna chahiye kya? Trade-off?
Production mein duplicate module copies kaise detect karoge?
Mutation testing ko CI mein reliable kaise banaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: `instanceof` strict aur type-safe hai lekin module identity pe depend karta hai. `name` ya brand symbol (`Symbol.for`) check cross-copy kaam karta hai lekin spoofable aur loose hai. Project ne instanceof rakha aur environment fix kiya.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Monorepo mein do packages library ki alag copies bundle karein: ek ka `BrokenCircuitError` doosre ke `isRetryableHttp` ko retryable lagega -- open breaker ke against retry storm. Yeh real failure mode hai jo is artefact ne dikhaaya.
advanced.alternatives: `Symbol.for('resilience-kit.BrokenCircuitError')` brand, `Symbol.hasInstance` override, ya package manager dedupe/peer dependency. Inme se kuch implement nahi hai.

advanced.production_improvements: Mutation runner ko normalized path (realpath) se chalana; CI mein ek 'known failures by name' diff; agar library publish ho toh brand-based checks socho.

question: A test expected a failure to be retried right after budget.canRetry() turned true again, and it failed. Was the test wrong or the code?
answer_hinglish:
Test galat tha, code sahi -- aur yeh finding README mein record hai: 'right after canRetry() turns true again, the next single failure is still not retried (found by a test that expected otherwise; the test now states it).'

Symptom: recovery test mein budget drain karke 0, phir 51 successes (5.1 tokens), `canRetry()` true. Test ne socha ab ek blip (pehla attempt fail, doosra ok) retry hoga aur 'ok' milega. Lekin promise 'blip' error se reject hua.

Investigation: retry.ts mein order padho: `shouldRetry` -> `budget.onFailure()` -> `maxAttempts` check -> `budget.canRetry()`. Blip ka pehla attempt fail hua, PEHLE token kata: 5.1 - 1 = 4.1. Phir `canRetry()`: 4.1 > 5? Nahi. Give up with reason 'budget'. `canRetry()` ka true hona sirf 'abhi is moment pe' tha, agle failure ke charge ke baad nahi.

Decision: code ko badlein ya test ko? Order intentional hai: failure real health signal hai, usko account karke decide karna conservative hai, aur outage simulation ka 1003 isi order pe based hai. Toh test ko sach bolne ke liye badla: ab woh assert karta hai ki 5.1 pe blip NOT retried, phir 21 successes aur (6.2, `toBeCloseTo(6.2, 10)`), aur tab blip retried (6.2 - 1 = 5.2 > 5). README ka 'after 51 ... 72 in total' wahi hai.

Lesson: jab test aur code disagree karein, pehle decide karo intended behaviour kya hai, phir jo galat hai usko theek karo. Aur us decision ko test mein comment ke saath likho taaki agla developer same confusion na kare.
why_needed: API ka naam (`canRetry`) ek promise jaisa lagta hai jo woh nahi deta. Aise semantics gaps production mein galat alerts aur galat expectations banate hain.
real_world_analogy: ATM balance Rs 510 dikhata hai aur minimum balance Rs 500 hai, toh lagta hai Rs 100 nikal sakte ho -- lekin transaction fee pehle kat-ti hai, toh nahi nikal sakte.
how_it_works: `canRetry()` sirf `tokens > max / 2` hai, side-effect free. Retry decision `onFailure()` ke BAAD hota hai, toh effectively retry ke liye failure ke waqt tokens > threshold + 1 chahiye.
in_this_project: `test/budget.test.ts` 'retries come back by themselves once the dependency recovers' -- comment: 'But the failing attempt itself costs a token BEFORE the check: 5.1 - 1 = 4.1, so a blip is still not retried.' `src/retry.ts::RetryPolicy` order. README RetryBudget paragraph.

Outage numbers (1003) consistent rehte hain

Recovery ke baad retries der se aate hain

question: Your breaker keeps opening although the dependency is up; most of its errors are HTTP 404. How do you investigate and fix it?
answer_hinglish:
Sabse likely cause: breaker default `isFailure` ke saath bana hai, jo HAR error ko failure maanta hai. Dependency 'record not found' pe 404 deti hai, `HttpError(404)` throw hota hai, aur breaker ki window mein woh failure gina jaata hai. 50% se zyada lookups missing records ke hon toh `minimumCalls` ke baad breaker open, aur ab saare calls -- valid wale bhi -- `BrokenCircuitError` paate hain.

Investigate kaise:
1. Events: `onEvent` handler mein `breaker-state` events log ho rahe hain (`from: closed, to: open`). Open hone ke time ke aas-paas dekho kaunse errors aaye.
2. `breaker.failureRate` getter metric mein dalo -- closed state ka current window rate.
3. Dependency ke errors ka `upstreamStatus` breakdown dekho: agar zyada 404/400/422 hain aur 5xx kam, toh classification galat hai.

Fix: `new CircuitBreaker({ isFailure: isRetryableHttp })`. `isRetryableHttp` network errors, timeouts, 408, 429, 5xx (501 chhod ke) ko failure maanta hai, baaki 4xx ko nahi. Ab 404 window mein SUCCESS gina jaata hai (dependency ne sahi jawab diya), lekin caller ko 404 wala `HttpError` phir bhi milta hai.

Proof: `test/http.test.ts` '404s do not open a breaker that uses isRetryableHttp as isFailure' -- real server 10 baar 404, breaker closed, server ne 10 hits dekhe. Aur README ka usage example khud `isFailure: isRetryableHttp` ke saath hai, comment 'a 404 is not "down"'.
why_needed: Galat failure classification breaker ka sabse common production bug hai: healthy service kaat di jaati hai aur outage tumhare hi breaker ne create kiya.
real_world_analogy: Smoke detector jo toast ke dhuaan pe bhi bajta hai -- dhire dhire log usko band kar dete hain. Sensor ko sahi cheez detect karni chahiye.
how_it_works: Default `isFailure` = `() => true`. Custom `isFailure(error) === false` -> outcome 'success'. Window ka failures count sirf real health failures pe badhta hai.
in_this_project: `src/breaker.ts` option `isFailure` (comment: 'A 404 or a validation error is the dependency answering correctly'), `src/http.ts::isRetryableHttp`, `src/events.ts` ka `breaker-state` event, `failureRate` getter. Test `test/http.test.ts` mein.
advantages: Ek option se fix, code change nahi
Events aur failureRate se diagnose possible
Retry aur breaker ka classification consistent
disadvantages: Default unsafe hai -- user ko yaad rakhna padta hai
Dependency agar galti se 4xx de (uska bug) toh breaker nahi bachayega
common_mistakes: Default isFailure production mein chhod dena
404 ko catch karke swallow karna taaki breaker na dekhe -- caller ko galat result milega
Breaker ko 'flaky' bolke uska threshold 0.9 kar dena bina root cause ke
