question: Add a queue timeout to the Bulkhead: a call that waits longer than maxWaitMs for a slot is rejected and leaves the queue. Write the change and a test.
answer_hinglish:
Aaj bulkhead ka waiter sirf do tarah queue chhod sakta hai: slot mil jaaye ya caller abort kare. Agar caller signal na de, ya de lekin kabhi abort na kare, toh woh unlimited wait karega. Queue timeout (`maxWaitMs`) yeh gap bharta hai -- is project mein implement NAHI hai, yeh exercise hai.

Design:
1. `BulkheadOptions` mein `maxWaitMs?: number` (validate: positive finite).
2. `Waiter` mein `timer` field.
3. `waitForSlot` mein ek common `leave(reason)` function: queue se splice, timer clear, abort listener remove, reject. Abort aur timeout dono `leave` call karte hain -- toh dono cleanup ek jagah, K7 jaisa leak dono raston pe band.
4. `release()` hand-off pe timer bhi clear kare (warna timer chalega aur already-resolved promise pe reject -- no-op, lekin timer process ko zinda rakhta hai: leak).
5. Rejection error: `BulkheadRejectedError` reuse kiya, taaki adapters ka 503 mapping aur `isRetryableHttp` ka 'not retryable' automatic kaam kare. Alternative: naya `BulkheadTimeoutError` -- clearer metrics, lekin har jagah mapping update.

Important: timeout rejection `await this.waitForSlot()` se aata hai, try/finally ke bahar, toh `release()` nahi chalta -- sahi, kyunki waiter ne slot kabhi liya nahi.

Tests (fake timers): (a) waiter 100 ms baad reject, `queued` 0, operation kabhi nahi chala, slot owner khatam hone par `running` 0; (b) slot time pe mil gaya toh koi timer pending nahi (`vi.getTimerCount()` 0) -- yeh leak test hai, K7 se seekha hua.
why_needed: Bounded queue bina bounded wait ke latency ko unbounded chhod deta hai. Caller ka SLA 2 s hai toh 10 s queue mein baithna bekaar hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ki waiting room: token mila lekin agar 30 minute mein number nahi aaya toh receptionist bol deti hai 'aaj nahi ho paayega, kal aao' -- unlimited baithne nahi deti.
how_it_works: Har waiter ka apna setTimeout. Teen exits: hand-off (release clears timer + listener), abort (leave), timeout (leave). Har exit baaki do mechanisms ko clean karta hai.
in_this_project: Change `src/bulkhead.ts` mein `BulkheadOptions`, `Waiter`, `waitForSlot`, `release`. Existing tests `test/bulkhead.test.ts` (controllable helper, listener spy test) pattern follow karo. README NOT implemented list mein queue timeout explicitly nahi hai, lekin code mein maxWaitMs jaisa koi option nahi hai.
advantages: Waiting time bounded: caller ke SLA se match
Ek `leave()` se saare exits ka cleanup consistent
Existing 503 mapping reuse
disadvantages: Har queued call ka ek timer -- thoda overhead
Same error type se metrics mein 'queue full' aur 'waited too long' alag nahi dikhte (event mein reason add karna padega)
common_mistakes: Hand-off pe timer clear na karna (timer leak)
Timeout pe `release()` call karna -- active galat ghatega
Timer aur abort dono fire hon toh double cleanup crash -- indexOf guard zaroori
follow_up_questions: Naya error type banaoge ya existing reuse? Kyun?
maxWaitMs aur andar ke TimeoutPolicy ka relation kya hona chahiye?
Queue wait time ka histogram kaise emit karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Error reuse (BulkheadRejectedError) vs naya type: reuse se adapters aur isRetryableHttp bina change kaam karte hain; naya type observability behtar karta hai. Per-waiter timer vs ek sweeper timer: per-waiter simple aur precise, sweeper lakhs waiters pe sasta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Timer aur hand-off same tick mein: agar timer pehle chala toh waiter queue se nikla aur release agle waiter ko deta hai; agar hand-off pehle hua toh timer clear. `indexOf` guard aur clearTimeout dono raston ko safe banate hain.
advanced.alternatives: Caller khud `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` pass kare (koi library change nahi) -- yeh aaj bhi possible hai! Isliye trade-off: built-in option convenience hai, zaroorat nahi. Ya deadline propagation: caller ka remaining budget pass karo.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade queues (hazaron waiters) pe per-waiter timers aur O(n) splice mehenge -- linked list aur ek timer wheel socho.
advanced.production_improvements: `bulkhead-rejected` event mein `reason: "queue-full" | "wait-timeout"`, aur queue wait time metric. Default maxWaitMs caller ke timeout se chhota.

question: The breaker's window is count-based only. Write a time-based window (last N seconds, in buckets) that the breaker could use instead, with a test showing old failures expire without new calls.
answer_hinglish:
Count-based window ki problem low traffic pe hai: PLAN kehta hai 'at low traffic the window can hold old outcomes'. 20 calls ka window, aur ghante mein 5 calls aati hain -- toh window mein 4 ghante purani failures baithi hain, aur ek naya failure breaker open kar sakta hai kyunki purani failures abhi bhi gini ja rahi hain. Time-based window 'last 10 seconds' ka rate deta hai, chahe kitne bhi calls hon. README: time-based window implement NAHI hai -- yeh exercise hai.

Design: bucketed ring (resilience4j ka time-based window bhi aise hi kaam karta hai -- generic knowledge, project se nahi). `buckets` count (jaise 10) aur `bucketMs` (jaise 1000) = 10 second window. Har bucket mein `calls`, `failures` aur `epochs[i]` -- woh kaunse time-slot ka data hold kar raha hai. Record: `epoch = floor(now / bucketMs)`, index `epoch % buckets`; agar `epochs[i] !== epoch` toh bucket purana hai, reset karo. Totals: sirf woh buckets jodo jinka `epoch - epochs[i] < buckets`. Isse expiry LAZY hai -- koi timer nahi, breaker ki 'no timer' philosophy ke saath consistent.

Breaker integration: `record()` ke closed branch mein ring buffer ki jagah `window.record(failed)`, phir `const { calls, failures } = window.totals()` aur same check `calls >= minimumCalls && failures / calls >= threshold`. `transition("closed")` mein `window.reset()`. 'ignored' aur generation logic waise hi.

Cost: totals() O(buckets) har call pe -- 10 buckets pe negligible; running sums se O(1) bhi kar sakte ho lekin expiry ke waqt adjust karna padega.
why_needed: Breaker ka decision 'abhi' ki health pe hona chahiye. Low-traffic dependencies (nightly jobs, rare admin APIs) pe count window 'abhi' ko nahi dikhata.
real_world_analogy: 'Last 20 deliveries ka rating' vs 'last 10 din ka rating'. Agar mahine mein 3 deliveries hon, toh pehla wala 6 mahine purani shikayatein dikhayega.
how_it_works: Bucket epoch tagging: bucket overwrite tab hota hai jab naya epoch uske index pe aaye. Stale buckets read time pe skip hote hain (`epoch - epochs[i] >= buckets`). Initial `epochs = -1`, aur calls 0 hain toh accidental inclusion harmless.
in_this_project: Aaj `src/breaker.ts` mein `ring`, `next`, `count`, `failures` count-based window hain aur `now` test hook already hai -- time-based window usi `now` ko use kar sakta hai. Tests `test/breaker.test.ts` ke `make()` helper ki tarah `now: () => t` se time control. README NOT implemented: 'The breaker's window is count-based only (no time-based window)'.
advantages: Low traffic pe bhi rate 'abhi' ka hai
Lazy expiry, koi timer nahi
Breaker ke existing `now` hook se testable
disadvantages: Bucket granularity: expiry bucketMs steps mein hoti hai, smooth nahi
totals() O(buckets) per call (running sums se O(1) possible)
Low traffic pe minimumCalls shayad kabhi poora na ho -- breaker kabhi open hi na ho
common_mistakes: Har call ka timestamp array mein rakhna (memory unbounded)
Read time pe stale buckets skip na karna -- sirf write time reset karna
Close pe window reset bhool jaana (B10 jaisa bug)
follow_up_questions: minimumCalls time-based window ke saath kaise behave karega low traffic pe?
Running sums ke saath O(1) totals kaise banaoge?
Clock jump (NTP adjust) pe kya hoga? `performance.now()` behtar hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Count-based: simple, O(1), traffic-independent memory, lekin low traffic pe stale. Time-based: 'abhi' ka rate, lekin minimumCalls low traffic pe kabhi poora nahi ho sakta aur bucket granularity tune karni padti hai. Hybrid: time window + minimumCalls dono.
advanced.failure_scenarios: `Date.now()` wall clock hai; NTP backward jump pe epoch peeche jaata hai aur buckets galat expire/reuse ho sakte hain. Monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) safer. Breaker ka current `now` default bhi `Date.now` hai -- wahi risk openMs pe bhi hai.
advanced.alternatives: Exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) failure rate -- ek number, smooth decay, buckets nahi. Ya per-call timestamps ka deque (exact, lekin memory traffic ke proportional).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x traffic pe har bucket bada number hold karta hai, memory same (buckets fixed) -- time window high traffic pe count window se behtar scale karta hai jahan 20 calls ka window milliseconds ka hota hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Window type ko option banao (`window: { type: "count" | "time" }`), slow-call rate saath mein (README NOT implemented), aur mutation checks naye window pe bhi (old failures expire, reset on close).

question: You already have a retry budget. Why do you still need a circuit breaker, and what does each one stop that the other cannot?
answer_hinglish:
Dono alag cheez limit karte hain. Budget RETRIES limit karta hai, breaker CALLS.

Budget ke saath outage mein bhi har incoming request dependency tak ek attempt bhejti hai. Simulation mein 1000 calls = 1003 attempts -- retries khatam, lekin 1000 attempts phir bhi gaye. Har attempt timeout tak wait karta hai (hanging dependency pe poore 2 s), caller ka latency kharab, sockets aur bulkhead slots bhare. Dependency ko recover karne ka time nahi milta kyunki traffic 1x pe chal raha hai.

Breaker open hone ke baad calls dependency tak JAATE HI NAHI. `http.test.ts` mein 20 calls open breaker ke saath server tak 0 baar pahunche -- 'the struggling server gets a rest'. Caller ko turant `BrokenCircuitError` with `retryAfterMs`, aur adapter usko 503 + Retry-After mein badal deta hai. Fail fast = low latency failure.

Breaker kya nahi kar sakta? Woh retries ko throttle nahi karta. Breaker closed hai (failure rate threshold se neeche, jaise 40%) toh har failed call ke 3 attempts jaayenge -- partial outage mein retries load ko 1.4x+ tak le jaate hain. Budget yahan adapt karta hai. Aur minimumCalls se pehle breaker koi decision nahi leta.

Composition mein ek important detail: breaker retry ke ANDAR hai, toh breaker har attempt dekhta hai (har failed attempt record hota hai: 10th failed attempt, 4th call ke dauraan, ise open karta hai; bahar hota toh sirf 4 outcomes, closed). Aur open breaker ka error `isRetryableHttp` ke liye non-retryable hai, toh retry turant rukta hai aur budget nahi chhoota.

Summary: budget = 'outage mein amplification band karo'; breaker = 'outage mein dependency ko bilkul chhod do aur jaldi fail karo'.
why_needed: Interviewer check karta hai ki tum har pattern ka exact role samajhte ho ya bas 'sab laga do' bolte ho. Overlap aur gaps dono batana senior answer hai.
real_world_analogy: Budget = 'ek baar hi call karo, baar baar nahi'. Breaker = 'abhi woh number band hai, call hi mat karo, 30 second baad try karna'.
how_it_works: Budget state: tokens, retry decisions pe. Breaker state: failure window + state machine, har call ke admission pe. Retry -> breaker order mein breaker ka BrokenCircuitError retry ke shouldRetry tak aata hai.
in_this_project: `src/budget.ts`, `src/breaker.ts`, `src/wrap.ts` comment. Tests: `test/budget.test.ts` (3000 vs 1003), `test/http.test.ts` 'circuit breaker: 503s open it, then requests stop reaching the server' (5 hits, phir 20 calls 0 hits, probe ke baad 6), `test/wrap.test.ts` 'breaker INSIDE retry sees every attempt' aur 'an open breaker inside retry (with isRetryableHttp) stops the retry at once' (0 retries).
advantages: Breaker: zero load + fast failure during outage
Budget: partial outage aur breaker-closed phase mein amplification control
Dono ek doosre ke signal ko distort nahi karte (non-retryable rejection)
disadvantages: Do mechanisms = do sets of tuning parameters
Breaker false opens ka risk laata hai jo budget mein nahi
Dono per-process
common_mistakes: Breaker ko retry ke bahar rakhna
Sochna budget hai toh breaker nahi chahiye (ya ulta)
Open breaker ke error ko retryable maanna (K9 mutation)
follow_up_questions: Partial outage (30% failures) mein kaun kya karega?
Kya breaker ka retryAfterMs retry ke Retry-After logic mein use hona chahiye?
Fallback (cached value) yahan kahan fit hoga? (implement nahi hai)

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Breaker: binary aur aggressive (sab band), budget: gradual (sirf retries band). Dono saath = outage mein zero load (breaker) aur grey failure mein bounded amplification (budget). Cost: zyada config aur interactions samajhne ki zaroorat.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Breaker threshold 50% aur dependency 45% fail kar rahi: breaker closed, har failure retry -- yahan sirf budget bachata hai. Ulta: dependency 100% down lekin traffic minimumCalls se kam -- breaker kabhi open nahi, budget hi limit karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Adaptive concurrency limit (latency-based), load shedding server side (dependency ke apne `loadShedding` jaisa), fallbacks -- adaptive concurrency aur fallback implement nahi hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x traffic pe breaker jaldi open hota hai (window fast bharta hai), budget jaldi drain -- dono better kaam karte hain. Lekin 100x replicas pe har replica alag seekhta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Ek dashboard pe dono: breaker state per dependency aur budget available; alerts give-up reason 'budget' aur 'breaker-rejected' rate pe.

question: The README lists adaptive concurrency and a slow-call rate as not implemented. If production showed the fixed bulkhead limit was wrong half the time, how would you evolve this design?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baseline: is project mein `Bulkhead` ka `maxConcurrent` fixed hai, aur breaker sirf errors ginta hai, slowness nahi (README: 'it has no "slow call" rate: put a TimeoutPolicy inside it so slow calls become failures'). Adaptive concurrency PLAN mein 'Not in scope' hai.

Fixed limit kyun galat hota hai? Dependency ki capacity badalti hai -- deploys, uske apne load, GC, region. Limit 20: dependency fast hai toh 20 bahut kam (throughput waste, bekaar rejections); dependency slow hai toh 20 bahut zyada (har call 2 s timeout tak latka, queue bhari). Little's law: concurrency = throughput x latency, toh latency double hui toh same throughput ke liye double concurrency chahiye -- ya limit wahi rakho aur throughput gira do.

Evolution, smallest step first:
1. Measure: har call ka latency aur `running`/`queued` metrics (events already hain; latency histogram add karo).
2. Slow-call rate breaker mein: outcome 'slow' agar duration > threshold, window mein alag counter, `slowRateThreshold` pe open. Breaker ke `record()` mein duration pass karna padega.
3. Adaptive limit: AIMD (additive increase, multiplicative decrease) -- har successful fast call pe limit +1/limit, timeout ya latency spike pe limit x 0.5. Ya gradient approach (Netflix concurrency-limits jaisa): min latency vs current latency ka ratio. `Bulkhead` mein `maxConcurrent` readonly hai -- usko mutable banana padega, aur limit ghatne par running calls ko kill nahi karte, bas naye admit nahi karte.

Direct hand-off design bachega: release ke waqt check 'active < currentLimit' tabhi hand-off, warna `active--`.

Risk: adaptive algorithms oscillate karte hain aur debug karna mushkil -- isliye pehle data, phir algorithm.
why_needed: Senior interview mein 'jo nahi banaya woh kaise banaoge' pucha jaata hai. Achha answer current limitation se shuru hota hai, measurement pe based hota hai, aur incremental hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Highway pe fixed speed limit vs smart signals jo traffic ke hisaab se lane kholte band karte hain. Smart signals behtar hain lekin galat sensor data pe chaos.
how_it_works: AIMD: TCP congestion control ka idea. Success pe slowly badhao, congestion signal (timeout, latency) pe tezi se ghatao. Bulkhead mein limit ek variable ban jaata hai jo har completion pe update hota hai.
in_this_project: Aaj ke hooks: `src/bulkhead.ts` mein `running`/`queued` getters aur `bulkhead-rejected` event; `src/breaker.ts` mein outcome model ('success'/'failure'/'ignored') jisme 'slow' add ho sakta hai; `src/timeout.ts` slow calls ko failure banata hai. README 'NOT implemented': 'Hedged requests, adaptive concurrency, fallbacks, caching' aur count-based-only window.
advantages: Limit dependency ki real capacity follow karta hai
Slow-call rate slowness ko breaker signal banata hai bina caller timeout tune kiye
Existing hand-off aur events design reuse
disadvantages: Oscillation aur tuning complexity
Testing mushkil: deterministic tests ke liye latency inject karni padegi
Per-process adaptive limits ek doosre se independent -- fleet level behaviour emergent
common_mistakes: Bina metrics ke adaptive algorithm laga dena
Limit ghatne par running calls ko cancel karna
Latency target ko p50 pe set karna -- normal variance pe hi limit gir jaayegi
follow_up_questions: AIMD vs gradient based limits -- kab kya?
Slow-call threshold aur TimeoutPolicy ms ka relation?
Adaptive limit ko kaise test karoge deterministically?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fixed limit: predictable, easy to reason, lekin capacity changes ko ignore karta hai. Adaptive: efficient, lekin non-deterministic aur oscillation-prone. Middle ground: fixed limit + good metrics + slow-call breaker, adaptive tabhi jab data dikhaye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Adaptive limit ek latency spike pe crash karke 1-2 pe aa jaaye aur dheere (additive) wapas aaye -- dependency theek ho chuki lekin hum minutes tak throttled. Ya GC pauses ko congestion samajh ke galat ghataye.
advanced.alternatives: Server-side load shedding (dependency khud 503 de), queue-based async processing (worker pool), hedged requests (tail latency ke liye; implement nahi). Ya simply dependency ke SLA ke hisaab se fixed limit + autoscaling.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x traffic pe fixed limit ka galat hona zyada costly hai (zyada rejections ya zyada pile-up). Adaptive per-process limits 100 replicas pe sab ek saath badhein toh dependency pe thundering herd -- jitter aur conservative increase zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Pehle latency histogram aur `running` gauge per dependency; phir slow-call rate breaker mein with mutation checks; adaptive limit feature flag ke peeche, ek dependency pe canary.

question: The README says to create one set of policies per dependency, once, and share it across calls. What breaks if you create them per request or share one set across dependencies?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag galtiyan, dono state ki wajah se.

Per request banana: breaker, bulkhead aur budget STATEFUL hain. Breaker ki window pichle calls yaad rakhti hai, bulkhead ka `active` sab concurrent calls ginta hai, budget ke tokens saare calls share karte hain. Har request pe `new CircuitBreaker()` = har breaker ka window khaali, pehla call hi uska ek-matra call -- `minimumCalls` (default 10) kabhi poora nahi hoga, breaker kabhi open nahi hoga. `new Bulkhead({ maxConcurrent: 20 })` har request pe = har request ka apna bulkhead jisme ek hi call -- limit kabhi lagti nahi. `new RetryBudget()` har request pe = har baar full bucket -- retry storm wapas (har call 3 attempts, simulation ka 3000). Code chalega, tests green, lekin protection zero. Sirf `TimeoutPolicy` aur `RetryPolicy` (bina budget) stateless hain, unko per call banana kaam karega lekin bekaar allocation hai.

Saari dependencies ke liye ek set: SMS provider down hua, uske failures breaker open karte hain -- aur ab payment gateway ke calls bhi `BrokenCircuitError` paate hain jabki woh healthy hai. Bulkhead ke 20 slots hanging SMS calls kha jaate hain, payment ko jagah nahi -- bulkhead ka poora isolation point khatam. Budget bhi SMS failures se drain hoke payment ke retries rok dega.

Isliye README: 'One set of policies PER DEPENDENCY, created once (module level / a singleton service), shared by every call.' NestJS mein yeh ek singleton provider ho sakta hai; Express mein module-level const, jaise README ka `sms` wrap.
why_needed: Sabse common resilience bug yahi hai: library sahi, wiring galat. Code review mein `new CircuitBreaker` ko request handler ke andar dekhna red flag hai.
real_world_analogy: Har ghar ka apna MCB (circuit breaker) hota hai, building ka ek common nahi -- warna ek flat ka short circuit poori building ki light kaat deta. Aur har baar switch on karte waqt naya MCB lagana bhi bekaar hai -- woh kuch yaad hi nahi rakhega.
how_it_works: Policy objects mein state: `CircuitBreaker` (ring, current, generation), `Bulkhead` (active, queue), `RetryBudget` (tokens). `wrap()` khud stateless hai -- sirf references hold karta hai -- toh ek baar banao aur reuse karo.
in_this_project: README 'Use it' section ka example: module level `const sms = wrap(...)` aur `sendSms` usko har call pe use karta hai. `src/budget.ts` comment: 'One budget per dependency, shared by every call to it.' `src/bulkhead.ts` comment: 'Limits how many calls to ONE dependency run at once'.
advantages: Har dependency ka failure isolated
State sahi accumulate hota hai, policies actually kaam karti hain
Names (`sms-breaker`) se events/metrics per dependency
disadvantages: Har nayi dependency ke liye config set banana padta hai
Per-process singletons -- replicas mein alag (README NOT implemented)
common_mistakes: Request handler ke andar `new CircuitBreaker()`
Ek global breaker sab dependencies ke liye
Ek dependency ke alag endpoints (fast read, slow report) ko ek hi bulkhead dena bina sooche
follow_up_questions: Ek dependency ke do endpoints ka behaviour bahut alag ho toh ek set ya do?
NestJS mein yeh policies kahan rakhoge?
Tests mein shared singleton state se isolation kaise rakhoge?

question: Design how you would share circuit-breaker and retry-budget state across many API replicas, given this library keeps it per process. Would you actually do it?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle clear: yeh project mein implement nahi hai. README: 'Anything shared between processes: a budget, a breaker and a bulkhead live in one process's memory.' PLAN: 'Distributed state (a breaker shared between processes through Redis)' not in scope. Toh yeh design discussion hai.

Mera recommendation: by default per-process rakho, aur shared state sirf ADVISORY banao, critical path pe nahi.

Kyun? Breaker har call pe check hota hai. Agar uska state Redis mein hai toh har call pe ek network hop (local check ~200-250 ns ka hai bench mein, Redis round trip typically sub-millisecond se millisecond tak -- generic ballpark). Aur bura: Redis slow ya down toh protection layer hi failure ban jaati hai. Resilience library ka naya single point of failure nahi hona chahiye.

Advisory design:
1. Har replica apna local breaker chalata rahe (aaj jaisa).
2. Jab local breaker open ho, woh Redis mein `breaker:sms = open until T` publish kare (TTL = openMs) -- fire and forget, errors ignore (jaise `emit` throwing handlers ignore karta hai).
3. Baaki replicas background mein (pub/sub ya har kuch second poll) yeh hint padhein aur apne breaker ko 'forced open until T' karein. Local decision hamesha valid; remote sirf jaldi open karata hai.
4. Half-open: probes coordinate karne ke liye Redis `SET NX` lock 'probe:sms' with TTL -- sirf ek replica probe bheje. Lock na mile toh local fallback.

Budget: sharing ka faayda kam hai -- har replica ka budget already apne traffic ke ratio pe adapt karta hai; outage mein extra cost sirf initial ~3 attempts per replica hai. Main share nahi karunga.

Bulkhead: global concurrency limit chahiye (dependency ka hard limit 50) toh Redis semaphore possible hai, lekin usually behtar hai per-replica limit = global / replicas, ya dependency ke saamne proxy.
why_needed: Distributed state ka sawaal har senior backend interview mein aata hai. Achha answer 'Redis laga do' nahi, balki cost, failure modes aur 'kya zaroorat bhi hai' discuss karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Har shop ka apna fire alarm (local breaker) + building ka WhatsApp group (advisory). Group pe message aaya 'third floor pe aag' toh tum bhi alert ho jaao, lekin group down ho toh bhi tumhara alarm kaam karta hai.
how_it_works: Local state machine authoritative; remote signal sirf 'force open' hint with expiry. Coordination primitives: TTL keys (expiry automatic), SET NX lock (probe election), pub/sub (fast propagation). Har remote op timeout ke saath aur failure pe ignore.
in_this_project: Aaj ke hooks jo design use karega: `onEvent` ka `breaker-state` event (publish trigger ke liye perfect -- open hone pe event aata hai), `BrokenCircuitError.retryAfterMs`, `CircuitBreaker` ka `now` aur `state`. Lekin 'force open' ke liye koi public API nahi hai -- `transition` private hai, toh library change chahiye. README NOT implemented aur PLAN Not in scope dono isko list karte hain.
advantages: Local fast path safe rehta hai, Redis outage protection nahi todta
Fleet jaldi seekhti hai ki dependency down hai
Probe coordination recovering dependency pe load kam karta hai
disadvantages: Naya infra dependency aur code complexity
Advisory = eventual; kuch calls phir bhi jaayenge
Library mein 'force open' API add karni padegi
common_mistakes: Har call pe Redis se breaker state padhna
Remote state ko authoritative banana -- network partition pe galat decisions
Budget bhi share karna jab zaroorat nahi
follow_up_questions: Network partition mein ek replica dependency tak pahunch sakta hai, baaki nahi -- shared breaker kya karega?
Probe lock holder crash ho jaaye toh?
Service mesh (Envoy) se yeh kaam karwaoge toh library ka kya role bachega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Authoritative shared state: consistent, lekin latency + naya SPOF. Advisory: fast aur resilient, lekin eventual. Pure per-process: simplest, fleet seekhne mein slow. Recommendation advisory, kyunki failure mode graceful hai (Redis gaya = aaj jaisa behaviour).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis split-brain ya stale key: ek healthy dependency ko 30 s ke liye sab replicas pe band kar de. TTL isko bound karta hai. Probe lock holder crash: TTL expire hone tak koi probe nahi -- TTL ko openMs ke order pe rakho. Network partition: ek replica ka 'open' baaki ke liye galat ho sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Service mesh outlier detection (Envoy) -- infra level per-host ejection, library ki zaroorat kam; client-side load balancer health checks; dependency ke saamne central proxy with global limits. Ya kuch nahi -- per-process enough hai zyaadatar cases mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10 replicas: per-process discovery cost (har replica ~minimumCalls failures) chhota. 100-1000 replicas: woh cost aur probes multiply hote hain, advisory sharing ki value badhti hai; Redis pub/sub fan-out bhi manageable. Global bulkhead semaphore 1000 replicas pe hot key ban sakta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Pehle metrics se measure karo kitni failed calls 'discovery' mein jaati hain per replica; agar significant ho tab advisory layer, feature flag ke peeche. Library mein minimal API add karo (`forceOpen(untilMs)`), mutation checks ke saath.
